solution: $\log_{p}q=\dfrac{\ln q}{\ln p}$. Multiply $R_1,R_2,R_3$ by $\ln2,\ln3,\ln5$ and divide $C_1,C_2,C_3$ by $\ln2,\ln3,\ln5$: the factors cancel, so $D$ is unchanged
Off-diagonal entries become $1$, diagonal entries stay $7$: $D=\begin{vmatrix}7&1&1\\1&7&1\\1&1&7\end{vmatrix}$
solution_full: By change of base, $\log_{p}q=\dfrac{\ln q}{\ln p}$, so the $(i,j)$ entry for $i\ne j$ is $\dfrac{\ln p_j}{\ln p_i}$ with $(p_1,p_2,p_3)=(2,3,5)$.

Multiply row $i$ by $\ln p_i$; the determinant is multiplied by $\ln2\cdot\ln3\cdot\ln5$. Then divide column $j$ by $\ln p_j$; the determinant is divided by the same product. So the value is unchanged.
After these operations the $(i,j)$ entry is $\dfrac{\ln p_j}{\ln p_i}\cdot\dfrac{\ln p_i}{\ln p_j}=1$ for $i\ne j$, and the diagonal entry is $7\cdot\dfrac{\ln p_i}{\ln p_i}=7$.
Apply $C_1\to C_1+C_2+C_3$ and take out $9$: $D=9\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&7&1\\1&1&7\end{vmatrix}$; then $R_2-R_1$, $R_3-R_1$ give $9\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\0&6&0\\0&0&6\end{vmatrix}=9\cdot36=324$.
(With diagonal $1$ instead of $7$ the matrix would have rank one and $D$ would be $0$.)
originality_note: New: the logarithmic matrix log_{p_i} p_j has rank one, but with 7 on the diagonal it becomes a rank-one perturbation; scaling rows by ln p_i and columns by 1/ln p_j turns it into [[7,1,1],[1,7,1],[1,1,7]] (way 4). Closest known: det[[1, log_x y, log_x z],[log_y x, 1, log_y z],[log_z x, log_z y, 1]] = 0. Different because: the diagonal is changed, the value is non-zero, and the reduction needs the row-column scaling property rather than proportional rows.
blueprint_concepts: Determinants with trigonometric or logarithmic entries

concept_use.Determinants with trigonometric or logar: The entries are logarithms to different bases; change of base writes each as ln p_j / ln p_i.
concept_use.Application of properties of determinant: Multiplying rows and dividing columns by the same numbers leaves the determinant unchanged; column addition then factors out 9.

stem_review: Read as a student: all logarithms are defined (bases 2, 3, 5); D is a fixed number; no ambiguity. Checked numerically with 15 digits: D = 324. Answer 324, a positive 3-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Scale row i by ln p_i and column j by 1/ln p_j to get the matrix with 7 on the diagonal and 1 elsewhere.
justification: A change of base and a row-column scaling property, then a standard determinant; routine chain without a new idea. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q8 (L2), logarithm manipulation.
